newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent crude firmer, US refiner dominates.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent crude firmer, US refiner dominates.

text.p: The North Sea Brent crude physical and paper markets were firmer on Tuesday with buying dominated by a U.S. refiner, traders said.
The refiner sold its August 12-14 Brent cargo at August Brent +4 cents, only to pick up an 13-15 loader, kept early from the paper chains, two cents cheaper.

Another 13-15 cargo was kept by the equity holder without being passed along the chains. No Brents from the August loading programme have so far been "clocked" or left unclaimed at five o'clock on the day they turn wet.
"It's not a storming market but I think (the wet market) can hold above August for a while longer," said one trader.

Dated Brent values plunged 17 cents on Friday to August flat but have since made a slight recovery. Traders said in the absence of Iraqi crude there was good demand for North Sea barrels at current levels.

The U.S. refiner active in the physical market was also the keenest bidder on paper, buying the September/October spread at a stronger -3 cents, two cents up from Monday's traded level. August/September was bid as high as +20 cents.
CFDs were also firmer with next week (August 4-8) traded at September flat and later weeks talked about 10 cents firmer.
September Brent was trading 13 cents up at $18.54 a barrel on the IPE screen at 1737 GMT, supported by a tight U.S. gasoline market.
